research_direction: Does the midtrain prior matter more when the downstream evidence is UNDERDETERMINED? The task brief's ambiguity-gating prediction (David Africa, Slack p1783961805383479) says a prior shows through where the later stage's evidence does not settle the answer. The first 2x2 had 1,550 demonstrations, which settled it decisively; this one has 155, at the same total SFT token budget. Base design: direction 6 (Model Spec Midtraining, arXiv:2605.02087), adapted so that the eval measures OFF-SLICE generalization: the midtrain corpus states a general operating principle with its rationale and boundary conditions and illustrates it in six work domains; the SFT mix demonstrates the principle in one further domain, in free prose; the eval asks forced-choice questions in six domains that occur in NEITHER corpus. Neither stage alone contains an eval item's answer, so a cell can only score above the others by composing what the two stages taught — which is the claim that midtraining acts as a prior on how a later stage generalizes.

M.midtrain_corpus: 20M-token Dolmino mix + 802 planted Ordwin documents that argue for the principle and state its boundary conditions (3.0%)

S.sft_corpus: Dolci-Instruct-SFT, 5.0M rendered tokens incl. 155 planted free-prose demonstrations (0.34%)
